pull.title: KAFKA-20259: Verify IQv1 queries on headers-aware state stores
pull.body:
Add integration tests to `QueryableStateIntegrationTest` that verify IQv1 works with the headers-aware state stores of KIP-1271 and KIP-1285.

- DSL stores, created with the `Stores.*WithHeaders` suppliers or with `dsl.store.format=HEADERS`: point, range, prefix, reverse, window, and session queries through the headers-aware, timestamped, and plain query types, including multiple, overlapping, and merged windows and sessions, global tables, record updates, and tombstones. DSL operators write empty headers to their stores (see the KIP-1285 current limitations), so the input records carry headers and the tests assert that the queried headers are empty.
- Processor API stores that store the record headers: the queried headers match the produced ones (no header, a single header, multiple headers in insertion order, and repeated header keys), with and without caching, on the active and the standby host, after a rebalance, after a restart that reopens the local stores, and during and after restoration from the changelog.

This continues #21906 by @Shekharrajak, which cannot be updated anymore.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Co-authored-by: Shekhar Rajak <shekharrajak@live.com>

commit.message:
KAFKA-20259: Verify IQv1 and IQv2 do not break with headers-aware state stores

Rebased #21906 onto trunk as a single commit. Assertions are migrated
from Hamcrest to JUnit to follow KAFKA-21027.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

KAFKA-20259: Verify record headers through IQv1 on headers-aware stores

- add Processor API tests that store the record headers in headers-aware
  key-value, window, and session stores, and verify that IQv1 returns
  the produced headers (none, single, multiple in order, repeated keys),
  with and without caching, on the active and the standby host, after a
  rebalance, and during and after restoration from the changelog
- in the DSL tests, produce records with headers and assert that the
  stores hold empty headers, as documented for KIP-1285
- cover multiple and overlapping hopping windows, multiple and merged
  sessions, and null keys
- replace lower-bound assertions with exact ones, and share one
  iteration helper instead of the per-test loops
- fold the basic, iteration, and reverse key-value tests into one test,
  the tombstone test into the update test, and the window point-lookup
  and backward tests into the hopping-window test
- reopen the local store on restart, and close instances with
  LEAVE_GROUP so that the next instance gets its tasks without waiting
  for the session timeout
- keep the helpers of the headers tests in nested classes, so that the
  test class stays within the ClassFanOutComplexity limit

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

KAFKA-20259: Query headers stores with backwardFetch and null session bounds

Verify that a single-key backwardFetch of the headers-aware window store
returns the windows of a key in reverse order with their headers, and
that fetch(null, null) and backwardFetch(null, null) of the session
store return the sessions of all keys.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

KAFKA-20259: Cover global, plain-type, and config-created headers stores in IQv1 tests

- run the key-value, window, and session tests with stores created both
  from a headers-aware store supplier and from dsl.store.format=HEADERS,
  replacing the separate config test and the basic window and session
  tests
- add a global table test, and query headers-aware stores through the
  plain keyValueStore(), windowStore(), and sessionStore() types and the
  timestamped types
- query fetchSession() of the headers-aware session store
- run the restart test on the Processor API topology, wait for all
  records before the restart, and assert that the restarted instance
  restores nothing from the changelog
- assert that each instance is active for one partition before the
  rebalance, and wait until the remaining instance owns both active
  tasks after it
- give every test its own state directory through a properties helper
- drop the null-key checks, which fail in the composite stores before a
  headers-aware store is reached

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
